body:
This story first appeared in Power Shift, The Yappie's weekly newsletter on national AAPI power, politics, and influence. Subscribe for free here.

Rep. Grace Meng (D-NY), chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), reintroduced a bill to make Diwali the 12th federally recognized holiday in the country.

  • The celebration, also known as the “Festival of Lights,” is celebrated by millions of Hindu, Buddhist, Sikh, and Jain people in America.

Our take: Though similar legislation died in Congress, escalating anti-South Asian hate has changed stakes in urgency, especially after authorities thwarted an alleged white supremacist’s plans for a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois. 

  • It’d remain largely symbolic without investments in programs to address the surge in violence, however.
  • Establishing Diwali as a federal holiday could signal to Americans—both Asian and not—that the U.S. government sees it as a part of shared civic life, according to lawmakers.
